newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high on HK handover eve.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high on HK handover eve.

text.p: Taiwan share prices salvaged a slight rise to notch another seven-year high close on Monday, fending off late profit-taking in electronics and jitters over Hong Kong's looming handover to Taipei's rival, Beijing.

The benchmark stock index surged as high as 9,131.86 points on window-dressing at the end of the first half, but saw the gains erode in late trade, managing only a scant gain of 5.80 points or 0.06 percent and a 9,030.28 point close.
The index has not closed higher since a 9,292.37 finish on April 30, 1990. Turnover was heavy at T$161.4 billion, but much lower than an all-time-high T$251 billion marked on June 19.
"Investors are concerned whether the Hong Kong handover ceremony can go smoothly," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.

"They also are watching whether China-related shares in the Hong Kong stock market can experience a further celebration rally after the July 1 handover," Chen said. Hong Kong's market reopens on July 3 after a long handover holiday.

Electronics rose 1.3 percent in early trade only to close with a 1.44 percent loss, as chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor failed to squeeze further gains from a 60.9 percent increase in its net profit target to T$14.72 billion.
Taiwan Semiconductor, which rocketed T$6 on Saturday, lost T$3 on Monday to close at T$123.5. The profit target raise was a sharp improvement but still well below its 1996 performance.
In 1996, Taiwan Semiconductor reported net profit of T$19.4 billion on sales of T$39.4 billion, up from T$15.08 billion on 1995 sales of T$28.77 billion.

"The sharp profit target increase failed to spark more gains on Taiwan Semiconductor, which in turn triggered overall profit-taking on electronics," said Jardine Fleming Securities fund manager George Hou.
